messages:
Deploy Bot: :rotating_light: deploy started by frida — rollout id 2026-03-15-6883, region=europe, strategy=blue-green, initial-weight=10%, ttl=300s
Alice (oncall): seeing elevated 5xx in eu-west canary dashboards, spike at ~10:14Z. rolling 10% of traffic but errors jump from 0.2% -> 6%.
Frida (engineer): ack. logs show KV cache cold misses and two OOMs on ml-infer-01. grabbing logs now.
Bob (eng-sre): paging Alice and Eli. pd-notif: PagerDuty incident PD-993 opened (P1) — "EU canary 5xx spike during rollout".
PagerDuty: Paging Alice (oncall) — severity P1 — please respond.
Alice (oncall): on it. can someone confirm if this is model runtime OOM or routing mismatch? I see inconsistent backend IPs returning 502/503.
Eli (infra-ops): checking LB health and DNS weights. early sign: route weights to green pool are 10% but some proportion of requests still hitting blue due to stale EDNS and our DNS TTL still at 300s.
Frida (engineer): confirmed that new sidecars are on green, but a subset of edge nodes cached old A records; request path ends up at older model variant which isn't compatible with new tokenizer changes -> 502.
Dan (CSM): any customer impact? any enterprise tenants seeing errors? I'm getting DM from account-squad.
Alice (oncall): preliminary: nonzero customer errors, most traffic from EU test clusters and a handful of customers hitting eu-west show increased error rates (~5-10% failed requests). not fully widespread yet.
Bob (eng-sre): immediate mitigation options: 1) kill rollout (feature-flag kill-switch) 2) force rollback to previous revision 3) lower DNS TTL and shift weight back to blue. fastest to stop customer impact is kill flag or rollback.
Frida (engineer): kill-switch is ready: `POST /flags/rollout-2026-03-15-6883/disable` — atomic and instantaneous for router config. rollback needs image revert which may take ~5-8 minutes.
Alice (oncall): I'm going to trigger the kill-switch. notify when done.
Frida (engineer): executing now:
```
# kill switch
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROUTER_TOKEN" https://controlplane.internal/flags/rollout-2026-03-15-6883/disable
```
Frida (engineer): done — controlplane ack: flag=disabled, rollout paused, traffic steering reverted.
Bob (eng-sre): router config shows immediate decrease in green pool weight -> 0%. requests should be back on blue.
Eli (infra-ops): confirming LB pools all healthy; synthetic checks from eu-west synthetic agents returning to 200 within 30s.
Alice (oncall): monitoring metrics... error rate decaying. looks like kill-switch worked.
Dan (CSM): pinging affected customers now: will send high-level note that we detected canary issues and paused rollout, investigating root cause.
Frida (engineer): follow-up: we saw incompatibility between model tokenizer change + older cached model variant on a subset of blue hosts. Need to ensure model variant compatibility check before route shift.
Bob (eng-sre): one more precaution: lowering DNS TTL to 60s would help future rapid weight flips. doing this now on eu-zone records (change applied to controlplane, propagation depends on caches). TTL set to 60.
Eli (infra-ops): note: some CDNs and enterprise resolvers ignore low TTLs; still helpful for our frontends.
Alice (oncall): PagerDuty: closing immediate P1 if metrics hold for 15m. leaving incident channel open for postmortem notes.
PagerDuty: Incident PD-993 updated: status mitigated -> monitoring.
Frida (engineer): collecting logs and core dumps, opening a bug: RNW-5123 "canary model-variant compatibility check". will attach repro and timeline.
Bob (eng-sre): action items for postmortem: 1) enforce pre-rollout compatibility checks (frida) 2) add automated validation of edge A record consistency (eli) 3) reduce default rollout TTL for region shifts or add explicit DNS flush guidance (alice/bob) 4) update runbook with kill-switch steps and commands (bob).
Dan (CSM): I'll follow up with affected accounts and share the customer impact window once we have timeline.
Alice (oncall): handing off to Bob for next shift — I'm going offline for the hour. Bob, you're primary for the next 2 hours.
Bob (eng-sre): taking handoff. I'll keep monitoring and coordinate the postmortem.
Frida (engineer): one more note: we should mark image compatibility in model manifest to avoid tokenizer mismatches. adding to RNW-5123.
Eli (infra-ops): monitoring DNS propagation, will report if any residual 502s persist.
Alice (oncall): final for now: impact contained, kill-switch executed at 10:16Z, error rates back to baseline by 10:18Z, P1 downgraded to monitoring at 10:30Z.
Bob (eng-sre): logged timeline and started incident ticket with attachments. will schedule postmortem for tomorrow 09:00 UTC.
Dan (CSM): thanks all. I'll draft customer comms and coordinate with solutions. :thumbsup:
Frida (engineer): nice response everyone. noted lessons and moving a compatibility gate into pre-deploy step.
Alice (oncall): closing thread update — follow-up task ownership in ticket RNW-5123 and incident board.
summary: EU canary rollout caused 5xx spike due to model-variant/tokenizer incompatibility plus DNS cache causing cross-pool routing; kill-switch used to pause rollout, TTL lowered, and follow-up actions created.
